title: Molecular screening for intestinal parasites
author: Chiara Piubelli

steps_raw.instruction: DNA extraction and molecular screening for intestinal parasites

According to the routine procedure of our laboratory, fecal samples collected for the molecular test were stored in 95% ethanol prior to processing. DNA extraction was performed by MagnaPure LC.2 instrument (Roche Diagnostic, Monza, Italy), using the DNA isolation kit I (Roche), as previously described (1). Molecular diagnostic screening for intestinal parasite was performed by three separate multiplex Rt-PCRs for Entamoeba histolytica - Entamoeba dispar - Cryptosporidium spp., for Giardia intestinalis - Dientamoeba fragilis - Blastocystis spp. and for Strongyloides stercoralis - Schistosoma spp - Hymenolepis nana. Multiplex Rt-PCRs were performed adapting the protocol reported by Verweij and colleagues (2, 3).
Multiplex real-time PCR

Amplification reactions for all the Rt-PCR were prepared in 25 µl, containing PCR buffer (SsoFast master mix, Bio-Rad Laboratories, Milan, Italy), 2.5 µg of BSA (Sigma-Aldrich, Milan, Italy), 5 l of sample DNA and a specific combination of primers and probe concentrations, depending on the performed multiplex. The Rt-PCR cycle protocol consisted of an initial denaturation step at 95 °C for 3 min, followed by 40 cycles at 95 °C for 15 s, 60 °C for 30 s and 72 °C for 30 s. Amplification, detection and data analysis were performed with the CFX 96 detection system (Biorad Laboratories) using white plates. Positive and negative controls were included in all the experiments. For each multiplex Rt-PCR, we used two positive controls: the first made by a DNA pool with low threshold cycle (Ct, Ct≤37) and a second one with high Ct (Ct>37). For all the Rt-PCR analyses, the threshold was set at 200. As a control for Rt-PCR inhibitors and amplification, the exogenous Phocine herpesvirus 1 DNA was amplified with the appropriate primers/probe mix in each multiplex Rt-PCR. The Rt-PCR targets are shown in table S1. Amplification reactions for all the Rt-PCR were performed adding 80 nM of each Phocine herpesvirus 1 (PhHV-1) specific primer and 200 nM of PhHV-1 CY5-BHQ2 labelled probe. Depending on the performed multiplex, we used the following combinations of primers/probes concentration:

300 nM of each G. intestinalis specific primer, 200 nM of G. intestinalis CY5.5-BHQ3 labelled probe. 100 nM of each D. fragilis specific primer and 100 nM of D. fragilis VIC-MGB labelled probe. 300 nM of each Blastocystis spp. specific primer and 100 nM of Blastocystis spp. FAM-MGB labelled probe.

60 nM of each E. histolytica/E. dispar specific primer and 200 nM of both E. histolytica FAM-MGB labelled probe and E. dispar VIC-MGB labelled probe. 200 nM of each Cryptosporidium spp. specific primer and 100 nM of Cryptosporidium spp. CY5.5-BHQ3 labelled probe.

80 nM of each Schistosoma spp. specific primer, 100 nM of each specific primer for both S. stercoralis e H. nana and 100 nM of the specific probe for each parasite (FAM- BHQ1 labelled probe for Schistosoma spp, CY5.5-BHQ3 for S. stercoralis and YY-BHQ1 for H. nana).
